confidence.reason: The bag field is clearly visible on a geo-referenced 2011 satellite image and its outline matches an April 2011 survey and the designers' own plan, so shape and position are well supported. But its area (0.40 ha) is only 40% of the roughly 1 hectare quoted by Wikipedia, Raised Water Research and a 2017 journal paper, and the rating scale asks for agreement within about 10%, so it is rated medium; the 13,000 m3 of sand fits 0.4-0.5 ha, which suggests the 1 ha figure is a loose envelope, but no source defines it.
factors: Structure clearly visible in Esri/Maxar imagery of 2011-09-28 (two years after completion, about five months after the first container failure) with the individual bag rows resolvable; re-checked with an independent per-channel stretch: outline within 1-3 px (0.4-1.1 m) on the W, E and S edges, up to ~4 px at the fuzzy north edge

Geo-referencing verified two ways: the outline converted to OSGB (E 411,435-411,514, N 90,838-90,937) lands on the reef in the geo-referenced April 2011 survey plot (IoU 0.77, centroids 8.5 m apart, 0.82 after a 5.6 m shift); the pier length measured on the image is 168-180 m against the stated 180 m
Independent April 2011 DGPS bathymetry plot (Rendle & Davidson 2012 Fig. 9) traced separately: 3,372 m2 (the faint deeper southern toe is excluded)

Designers' numerical design shape (Mead et al. 2010 Fig. 3a) traced: 4,217 m2, 110 x 49 m rotated rectangle vs satellite 4,042 m2, 121 x 45 m; the design relief footprint (>0.5 m above ambient seabed, measured by the verifier) is 5,255 m2 and holds 11,540 m3 of sand against the 13,000 m3 stated
Shore-normal bearing measured on the image (173.4 deg) equals the 173 deg the Plymouth paper uses; reef west edge 242 m east of the pier head vs 'about 240 m' in the text

Why not high: rubric requires dimensions within ~10% of the text. Text areas: about 1 ha (Wikipedia, Raised Water Research, Herbert et al. 2017 - unreferenced), 'football pitch', 45,000 m2 (Rendle & Davidson), 50 x 70 m (unverified snippet). Drawn bag field 4,042 m2 is -60% against 1 ha; the shore-aligned bounding box (88 x 94 m = 0.83 ha) is -17%

Why the drawing is probably right and the 1 ha probably loose: 13,000 m3 over 4,042 m2 is 3.2 m mean thickness (two container layers, 4.5-5.5 m relief), over 1 ha it would be 1.3 m; three independent plan-view sources give 3,400-4,200 m2

Edges are visible-edge traces through 2-5 m of turbid water: +/- 3 px (about 1 m) at the clear W/E/S edges, softer at the north edge and the south toe; the true toe of the sand-filled bags is a few metres outside the visible edge (a 5 m skirt would give 5,573 m2)

design_version.drawn: As-built outer envelope of the two-layer geotextile-container reef (construction finished Sept-2 Oct 2009), as imaged on 2011-09-28: i.e. after the April 2011 damage (one 70 m container emptied, about 80 t of sand lost, 4 m gap, 2 m crest dip) and while the contractor's repair crew was back on site (from mid-Aug 2011); the planned Dec 2010 extension is not documented as built (Rendle & Davidson, Aug 2012: no works took place). The traced line is the outer edge of all visible bag rows.
design_version.why_this_one: It is the built structure seen directly: a post-construction satellite image of known date (capture date checked at four points of the Wayback metadata layer), confirmed by the April 2011 survey. No later redesign or rebuild exists: the reef closed on 31 March 2011; the council announced ASR's return on 12 Aug 2011 (repair of two upper-layer containers; improvement money redirected to repair) and said on 24 Oct 2011 that repairs would continue into spring 2012, but Rendle & Davidson (Aug 2012) state that neither works nor repairs took place; ASR was liquidated in Sept 2012 and the council then repurposed the reef as a dive/activity site without enhancing it. Repairs concern containers inside the envelope, so the plan outline is the same either way. A satellite image or survey of the built reef outranks the designers' drawing.

gemini.summary: Gemini's Boscombe shape is an 'asymmetric triangular delta' of 100 x 55 m / 5,200 m2 (net 3,070 m2), with a second, inconsistent quadrilateral of 9176 m2 (171 x 88 m) in its JSON; its three named sources have no URLs and could not be found, and the one real photo it cites does not support its claims. Our traced bag field is a 121 x 45 m elongated band of 4042 m2 whose long axis lies 55 deg from the shoreline; Gemini's 220 m offshore is the only number that fits. Verification 2026-10-05: all six verdicts re-checked and confirmed; Gemini's own reef_footprints.json text calls its 9,180 m2 the 'full calibrated GSC ramp envelope (~1.0 ha / 2.5 acres)', i.e. fitted to the 1 ha text, and 5,200 / 3,070 m2 come from its own CAD sketch ('Original Hydrodynamic & Bathymetric Synthesis').
